cohort: A total of 18,093 women admitted for assistance at delivery in a 5-year period (2012-2016) were included in the analysis.
finding: Increases in maternal age at delivery are associated with higher healthcare costs, driven largely by additional complication rates, irrespective of the delivery mode.
mod_finding: Uncomplicated vaginal deliveries decreased across increasing maternal age groups, while a three-fold risk of cesarean section complications was calculated in women over 45 years-old compared to those under 20 years of age.
